title: Finite bases pass to completed constant quotient sheaves
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $A\to B$ a homomorphism of commutative rings, and $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ an $A$-basis of $B$, with $d\geq0$. Let $t\in A$, $v\in B$, $u\in B^\times$ and $e\geq1$ satisfy $t=u v^e$ in $B$. Write $\underline{M}$ for the constant sheaf associated to an abelian group or ring $M$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Put $R=\lim_{n\geq1}\underline{A/t^nA}$ and $S=\lim_{m\geq1}\underline{B/v^mB}$. There is a unique ring map $R\to S$ whose $m$-th projection is $R\to\underline{A/t^mA}\to\underline{B/v^mB}$. Inverse limits are sectionwise [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. The basis maps on the quotients induce an $R$-linear isomorphism $R^{\oplus d}\xrightarrow{\sim}S$, with $i$-th column the compatible residues of $b_i$. For every $n\geq1$, its projection at $m=en$ is the composite $R^{\oplus d}\to\underline{A/t^nA}^{\oplus d}\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{B/t^nB}=\underline{B/v^{en}B}$, where the first map is coordinatewise projection and the second is the quotient basis isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), pp. 58-59: inverse limits of constant quotient sheaves. The basis and cofinal-filtration refinement below is an agent argument, not a numbered assertion of the source.

proof.text: Write $b:A^d\to B$, $(a_i)\mapsto\sum_i a_i b_i$, and let $c_i:B\to A$ be its coordinate maps. For each $n\geq1$, $b((t^nA)^d)=t^nB$: one inclusion is $\sum_i t^na_ib_i=t^n\sum_i a_ib_i$, and conversely the coordinates of $t^nx$ are $t^nc_i(x)$. Consequently $q_n:(A/t^nA)^d\to B/t^nB$, $([a_i])\mapsto[\sum_i a_ib_i]$, is well defined with inverse $[x]\mapsto([c_i(x)])$. These maps are $A/t^nA$-linear. Reducing from level $n+1$ to $n$ commutes with both formulas, since reduction leaves the representatives and the coordinate maps unchanged. The argument includes $d=0$: then the assumed basis isomorphism identifies the underlying module of $B$ with zero.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), pp. 58-59, inverse-limit coefficient construction; elementary basis/cofinal-filtration refinement written by NS.

proof.text: Apply constant presheaves and sheafification to $q_n$ and its inverse; by [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] the resulting objects are the constant sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact], sheafification commutes with finite products, giving the canonical identification $\underline{(A/t^nA)^d}=\underline{A/t^nA}^{\oplus d}$ (finite products and sums of modules have the same coordinatewise operations). Apply [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] with the constant ring presheaf $\mathcal O=A/t^nA$: it supplies the module actions and makes the sheafified maps $\underline{A/t^nA}$-linear. Its target is the abelian sheafification $P^\#$ of the constant presheaf $P=B/t^nB$; regard the ring sheaf $\underline{B/t^nB}$ as an $\underline{A/t^nA}$-module through the sheafified ring map. The ring-sheafification unit $P\to\underline{B/t^nB}$ is $\mathcal O$-linear, so by the same lemma it factors as $P\to P^\#\xrightarrow{\varphi}\underline{B/t^nB}$ with $\varphi$ linear. By [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets], in both its abelian-group and its commutative-ring case, both units exhibit the set sheafification of $P$, so $\varphi$ is bijective. Composing with $\varphi$, $\beta_n:\underline{A/t^nA}^{\oplus d}\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{B/t^nB}$ is an isomorphism onto the ring sheaf, linear for the action through the ring map, whose columns are the residues of the $b_i$. Functoriality preserves the commuting reduction squares of step 1, so the $\beta_n$ and their inverses commute with all transition maps.

proof.text: In $B$ one has $t^n=u^n v^{en}$, and multiplication by the unit $u^n$ gives $t^nB=v^{en}B$. Also $t^mB\subseteq v^mB$, since $em\geq m$. Hence $A\to B$ induces compatible ring maps $f_m:A/t^mA\to B/v^mB$: both composites from level $m+1$ send the class of $a$ to its image in $B/v^mB$. Use [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] to sheafify these maps. For $r=(r_n)\in R(U)$ set $f(r)_m=\underline f_m(U)(r_m)$. The transition equality makes this a compatible family; [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] identifies it with a section of $S(U)$. Componentwise it preserves the ring operations and restrictions. This constructs the required ring-sheaf map $f:R\to S$, and every map with the prescribed projections has exactly these coordinates, proving uniqueness.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), pp. 58-59, inverse-limit coefficient construction; elementary basis/cofinal-filtration refinement written by NS.

proof.text: Put $T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\underline{B/t^nB}=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\underline{B/v^{en}B}$. The equality of ideals in step 3 identifies the transition maps as well as the quotients. The sectionwise limit description [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] gives $h:S\to T$, $h(s)_n=s_{en}$. Its inverse sends a compatible family $z=(z_n)$ to the family whose $m$-th component is the reduction of $z_m$ from $B/v^{em}B$ to $B/v^mB$. For $m+1\to m$ these components agree by reducing the transition equality for $z_{m+1}\to z_m$ further to $v^m$. For $s\in S$, the reconstructed component is $s_{em}\bmod v^m=s_m$. For $z\in T$, the $n$-th component of $h(h^{-1}(z))$ is $z_{en}\bmod v^{en}=z_n$, by the transition from index $en$ to index $n$. Thus both composites are identities. All formulas preserve addition, multiplication and restrictions.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), pp. 58-59, inverse-limit coefficient construction; elementary basis/cofinal-filtration refinement written by NS.

proof.text: Use [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] and step 2 to define $\Phi:R^{\oplus d}\to T$: for $r_i=(r_{i,n})_n$, put $\Phi((r_i)_i)_n=\beta_n((r_{i,n})_i)$. Compatibility of the $\beta_n$ makes this a compatible family. Conversely, for $z\in T(U)$ apply $\beta_n^{-1}$ to $z_n$; their compatibility says that for each $i$ the $i$-th coordinates form a section $r_i\in R(U)$. These operations are inverse, commute with restrictions, and preserve addition. The finite direct sum here is the sheaf with section module $R(U)^d$: the coordinate inclusions and projections give its coproduct universal property, since a map out of it is the finite sum of its composites with those inclusions. This also treats the empty sum $d=0$. Hence $\Psi=h^{-1}\Phi$ is an additive sheaf isomorphism $R^{\oplus d}\cong S$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), pp. 58-59, inverse-limit coefficient construction; elementary basis/cofinal-filtration refinement written by NS.

proof.text: For $a\in R(U)$ the $n$-th coordinate of $h(f(a))$ is $\underline f_{en}(a_{en})$, and it equals the image of $a_n$ in $\underline{B/t^nB}(U)$: the map $A/t^{en}A\to B/v^{en}B=B/t^nB$ factors through $A/t^nA$, and $a_{en}$ reduces to $a_n$. Thus the $R(U)$-action on $T(U)$ transported through $h$ acts at index $n$ through $a_n$. The $\underline{A/t^nA}$-linearity of $\beta_n$ gives $\Phi(a(r_i))_n=a_n\Phi((r_i))_n$. Equality in the sectionwise limit now proves $\Psi(a(r_i))=f(a)\Psi((r_i))$; by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] this is $R$-linearity. Applied to the $i$-th coordinate unit vector, $\Phi$ has coordinate $b_i\bmod t^n$; the formula for $h^{-1}$ then gives $b_i\bmod v^m$ in every component $m$. Finally $h\Psi=\Phi$ says precisely $\pi_{en}\Psi=\beta_n\circ(\pi_n)^{\oplus d}$. This proves the specified columns and the corrected projection factorization, without asserting that the completion projection itself is an isomorphism.
